newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama grants asylum to Ecuador's deposed Bucaram.
newsitem.headline: Panama grants asylum to Ecuador's deposed Bucaram.

text.p: Ecuador's deposed President, Abdala Bucaram, was granted political asylum in Panama, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday.

"The government of Panama has given political asylum to Bucaram, his wife, children and brother, effective last Thursday," spokesman Erich Rodriguez said. The measure covered Bucaram's wife, Rosa Maria Pulley, their four children Jacobo, 18, Linda, 17, Abdala 15, and Michelle, 13, and Bucaram's brother, Santiago, who was expelled from Ecuador's Congress.

Bucaram was deposed by Congress on Feb. 6 on grounds of "mental incompetence" after only six months in office and travelled to Panama a few days later. The populist leader, known as "el loco" (the crazy one) for his eccentric personal style, had lived in exile in Panama from 1985-90 after fleeing charges of corruption as mayor of his home city, Guayaquil.

News that Bucaram's asylum request was granted coincided with a peaceful protest staged by a small group of Ecuadorans inside Ecuador's Embassy in Panama City. "We are against Panama giving Bucaram asylum," Emma Ortega, leader of a group of seven people, said.
She said they flew in from Ecuador on Monday to stage the protest. "Bucaram is an assassin," she told reporters without giving details about her group.

Ecuador's Supreme Court has issued a warrant for Bucaram's arrest on grounds of misuse of presidential funds. Congress has expelled 13 deputies, including his brother, who was accused of siphoning funds from the national budget.
